source_row.rationale: Sharp pleuritic positional chest pain that improves when sitting up or leaning forward, together with a pericardial friction rub, is characteristic of acute pericarditis, so Option B is correct. Myocardial infarction, pulmonary embolism, and gastroesophageal reflux can cause chest discomfort but do not account for the characteristic pericardial friction rub plus this positional pain pattern.
source_row.source_detail: StatPearls Pericarditis — History and Physical: acute pericarditis classically causes severe pleuritic, positional chest pain that improves with sitting up and leaning forward; examination may reveal a pericardial friction rub. Current StatPearls/NCBI Bookshelf Pericarditis entry, updated 2026-04-13; live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Physiological Adaptation: acute/complex alterations, endocrine/vascular emergencies and pathophysiologic adaptation. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
source_row.stem: A client has sharp pleuritic chest pain that worsens when lying flat and improves when leaning forward, and a pericardial friction rub is heard. Which condition is most likely?
